name.hi: वायु की उपस्थिति और गतिशील वायु
ऑक्सीजन का संतुलन और पवन ऊर्जा

hi.concept: इस अध्याय में हमारे चारों ओर वायु की उपस्थिति, वायु की संरचना और उसके विभिन्न घटकों का अध्ययन किया जाता है। ऑक्सीजन respiration और burning के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है। जलवाष्प, धूल और smoke भी वायु में पाए जा सकते हैं। अध्याय यह भी समझाता है कि वायु पानी और मिट्टी में उपस्थित है तथा plants oxygen के संतुलन में योगदान करते हैं।
hi.example: एक खाली दिखाई देने वाली बोतल को पानी में तिरछा करने पर bubbles निकलते हैं, जिससे बोतल में वायु की उपस्थिति दिखाई देती है। फिरकी का घूमना moving air का प्रभाव दिखाता है।

examTraps.title: वायु दिखाई देती है या नहीं
examTraps.fact: वायु सामान्यतः दिखाई नहीं देती, लेकिन उसकी उपस्थिति महसूस और प्रदर्शित की जा सकती है।
examTraps.confusion: हवा को न देख पाने का अर्थ यह नहीं कि वह मौजूद नहीं है।

examTraps.title: Nitrogen और oxygen
examTraps.fact: Nitrogen वायु का सबसे बड़ा घटक है, जबकि oxygen burning और respiration support करती है।
examTraps.confusion: सबसे अधिक मात्रा में होना और burning support करना अलग गुण हैं।

examTraps.title: Water vapour और droplets
examTraps.fact: Water vapour gas है और ठंडी सतह पर condense होकर droplets बना सकती है।
examTraps.confusion: दिखाई देने वाली बूंद को सीधे water vapour न समझें।

examTraps.title: Air in water
examTraps.fact: पानी में dissolved air होती है, जिसे heating पर bubbles के रूप में दिखाया जा सकता है।
examTraps.confusion: ब bubbles को पानी की अपनी gas न मानें; वे dissolved air से आ सकते हैं।

examTraps.title: Air in soil
examTraps.fact: Soil particles के बीच spaces में air हो सकती है।
examTraps.confusion: मिट्टी को पूरी तरह solid और air-free न मानें।

examTraps.title: Wind और wind energy
examTraps.fact: Moving air को wind कहते हैं और उसकी energy का उपयोग windmills कर सकती है।
examTraps.confusion: Wind और wind energy को एक ही शब्द न मानें।

en.concept: This chapter studies the presence of air around us, its composition and its different components. Oxygen is important for respiration and burning. Water vapour, dust and smoke can also be present in air. The chapter also explains that air is present in water and soil and that plants contribute to the balance of oxygen.
en.example: When an apparently empty bottle is tilted under water, bubbles escape, showing that air was inside. A firki rotating demonstrates the effect of moving air.

sections.title: Presence and Moving Air
sections.concept: Air is present all around us.
sections.explanation: This section explains the related facts, activities and scientific conclusions from the chapter.
sections.example: Air usually cannot be seen, but its presence can be felt.
keyPoints: Air is present all around us.
Air usually cannot be seen, but its presence can be felt.
Moving leaves show the effect of moving air.
Clothes fluttering in air are an example of moving air.
Pages of a book can move when a fan is switched on.

sections.title: Composition of Air
sections.concept: Air is not a single substance but a mixture of several components.
sections.explanation: This section explains the related facts, activities and scientific conclusions from the chapter.
sections.example: Nitrogen is present in the largest amount in air.
keyPoints: Air is not a single substance but a mixture of several components.
Nitrogen is present in the largest amount in air.
The amount of oxygen in air is less than nitrogen.
The old NCERT chapter describes nitrogen as about four-fifths of air.
The old NCERT chapter describes oxygen as about one-fifth of air.

sections.explanation: This section explains the related facts, activities and scientific conclusions from the chapter.

keyPoints: Green plants release oxygen during photosynthesis.
Plants use carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
Living organisms take in oxygen during respiration.
Carbon dioxide is released during respiration.
Photosynthesis is important in the balance of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Air is present all around us and occupies space.
Moving air is called wind.
Air is a mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour and other components.
Oxygen is needed for respiration and supports burning.

examTraps.title: Can air be seen
examTraps.fact: Air is generally invisible, but its presence can be felt and demonstrated.
examTraps.confusion: Not seeing air does not mean that it is absent.

examTraps.title: Nitrogen and oxygen
examTraps.fact: Nitrogen is the largest component of air, while oxygen supports burning and respiration.
examTraps.confusion: Being present in the largest amount and supporting burning are different properties.

examTraps.title: Water vapour and droplets
examTraps.fact: Water vapour is a gas and can condense into droplets on a cool surface.
examTraps.confusion: Do not treat visible droplets as water vapour itself.

examTraps.title: Air in water
examTraps.fact: Water contains dissolved air, which can be seen as bubbles when water is heated.
examTraps.confusion: The bubbles can come from dissolved air in the water.

examTraps.title: Air in soil
examTraps.fact: Air can be present in spaces between soil particles.
examTraps.confusion: Do not assume soil is completely solid and air-free.

examTraps.title: Wind and wind energy
examTraps.fact: Moving air is wind and windmills can use its energy.
examTraps.confusion: Wind and wind energy are related but are not the same term.
